summary: At conservation level, the EU LULUCF framework sets a -310 Mt CO2-eq carbon-sinks target by 2030, associated with 42 Mt CO2-eq of additional net removals versus 2016–2018. For restoration, at least 20% of EU land areas and 20% of EU sea areas should have restoration measures by 2030, and all ecosystems needing restoration should have such measures by 2050. Peatland and wetland rewetting/restoration is associated with 51–54 MtCO2-eq/yr of potential, while the mixed restoration/conservation measure combining reforestation respecting ecological principles for biodiversity with sustainable forest management has 8–235 MtCO2-eq/yr potential. Agriculture seeks better fertiliser-use efficiency, with 19 MtCO2-eq/yr potential. No Germany-specific allocation is supplied. Germany has 114,594 km² of forest (32.1%), 53,035 km² of grassland (14.9%), 939 km² of wetland (0.3%), and 161,364 km² of agriculture (45.2%), but these EU-level or non-area figures cannot establish the national share covered.

targets.context: EU-level target; the passage associates it with 42 Mt CO2-eq of additional net removals relative to 2016–2018, but gives no Germany allocation.

targets.metric: Minimum share of EU land areas with restoration measures
targets.context: The denominator is total EU land area; Germany’s 357,013 km² is not the stated denominator, and no national allocation is provided.

targets.metric: Minimum share of EU sea areas with restoration measures
targets.context: The denominator is total EU sea area; no Germany-specific marine share is stated.

targets.metric: Peatland and wetland restoration mitigation potential (range lower bound)
targets.context: The reported range is 51–54 MtCO2-eq/yr; the value field records its lower bound. This is an EU mitigation-potential total, while Germany’s wetland class is 939 km²; no national allocation is stated.

targets.metric: Reforestation and sustainable forest management mitigation potential (range lower bound)
targets.context: The reported range is 8–235 MtCO2-eq/yr; the value field records its lower bound. No reforestation area is assigned against Germany’s 114,594 km² of forest.
No share of Germany’s 161,364 km² of agricultural land is specified; the figure is mitigation potential rather than covered area.
